title: EU AI Act deadlines moved, and the dates are worth getting right
angle: The timeline shifted, which is exactly the kind of thing people repeat incorrectly. Useful to lay out plainly, including the part that is still not settled.
keyPoints: The European Parliament voted to delay key compliance deadlines, pushing high risk AI system requirements to December 2027, and to August 2028 for sector specific obligations.
That delay is not fully settled: the Council of the EU still needs to agree for it to take legal effect before the original 2 August 2026 date.
Article 50 transparency obligations apply from 2 August 2026, which covers chatbot transparency.
Transparency requirements for AI generating synthetic audio, image, video or text moved to 2 December 2026.
Two new prohibited practices apply from 2 December 2026: nudifier applications, and AI generated child sexual abuse material.
The Act is not retroactive, so systems already on the market before it takes effect may be exempt from some obligations.
